parameters are selected to investigate the low-SNR regime,
in which the effective received SNRs at both Bob and Eve
remain small. Without loss of generality, we adopt a simplified
spatial correlation model inspired by [15], [16], where the
eavesdropping and legitimate channels are partially correlated
due to shared scattering in the propagation environment. We

In order to study the performance, we evaluate three algo-
rithms which are as follows:
1) Alg. 1 is a Bob-centric design that configures the BD-RIS
scattering matrix to maximize Bob’s received power by
using only the MRT design, without explicitly accounting
for Eve [11, Eq. (23)].
2) Alg. 2 is the BD-RIS secure design that starts from
the MRT-based BD-RIS configuration and adjusts the
scattering matrix to preserve a large received power at
Bob while simultaneously suppressing Eve via nulling
[11, Algorithm 1].
3) Alg. 3 is the proposed channel difference-centric design
in Sec. III.
We first examine MISO systems aided by different BD-RIS
architectures considering selecting the antenna that maximizes
the upper bound on Bob’s channel gain (16). In Fig. 2, we
compare the secrecy rate performance versus the number of

Bob-Eve channels. For ρ = 0, the secrecy rate increases with
the RIS size. The proposed algorithm achieves secrecy rates

close to those of MRT with Eve-nulling, particularly for larger
RIS sizes. Here, Eve-nulling incurs only a modest loss in Bob’s
channel gain. For ρ = 0.9, MRT yields approximately zero
secrecy rate because enhancing Bob’s channel also strengthens
Eve’s link. MRT with nulling eliminates leakage but sacrifices
substantial Bob-channel gain due to the overlap between the
channel directions. By balancing Bob-channel enhancement
and Eve leakage rather than enforcing strict nulling, the
proposed algorithm achieves a higher secrecy rates over the
considered range.
Fig. 3 shows that, at ρ = 0.9, increasing transmit power
improves the secrecy rates of the proposed design and MRT
with nulling, whereas MRT remains near zero. The proposed
design achieves a better secrecy tradeoff by allowing residual
leakage when offset by greater Bob-channel gain, although
its advantage over nulling is relatively small for FC. In both
figures, the performance ordering is FC, GC-4, GC-2, and SC.
Fig. 4 shows the impact of Bob-Eve channel correlation with
NI = 44 and Pt = 15 dBm. At low correlation, the proposed
design and MRT with nulling achieve comparable secrecy
rates. As ρ increases, MRT approaches zero secrecy rate, while
the proposed design outperforms MRT with nulling, since
strict Eve-nulling sacrifices useful Bob-channel gain when the
channel directions strongly overlap.
Fig. 5 (a) illustrates the impact of the number of Alice
antennas, NA, under strong Bob-Eve channel correlation,
ρ = 0.9. As NA increases, the proposed algorithm achieves
an increasing secrecy rate for all BD-RIS architectures. In
